OpenCode and Copilot cannot load this project's plugin / skill / MCP runtime on their own. cli-opencode is the documented bridge that lets a OpenCode-led orchestration call into the project's spec-kit workflows without leaving the OpenCode session.

---

## 5. SMART-ROUTER DECISION TREE

The skill's smart router picks between the three use cases (or refuses) using this decision tree:

```text
INPUT: prompt + calling runtime
                |
                v
[ADR-001 SELF-INVOCATION GUARD]
- Layer 1: env var lookup (any OPENCODE_* env var present?)
- Layer 2: process ancestry (opencode in parent process tree?)
- Layer 3: best-effort lock-file probe (~/.opencode/state/<id>/lock present? -- heuristic, not guaranteed on every install)
                |
        +-------+-------+
        |               |
       NO              YES
        |               |
        v               v
[CALLING RUNTIME]   [PROMPT KEYWORDS]
        |               |
        |               +-- parallel words ......... USE CASE 2 (in-OpenCode parallel)
        |               +-- self-dispatch only ..... REFUSE (cycle — surface ADR-001 error)
        |
        +-- Anthropic (Claude Code) ............... USE CASE 1 (external to OpenCode)
        +-- Other (OpenCode Copilot)
                |
                v
        [PROJECT SUBSYSTEM NAMED?]
                +-- YES ........................... USE CASE 3 (cross-AI handback)
                +-- NO ............................ USE CASE 1 (external to OpenCode)
```

### Refusal message

When the router hits the REFUSE leaf, it surfaces this exact message:

```text
ERROR: cli-opencode self-invocation refused.

You are already inside OpenCode (signal: <env|ancestry|lockfile> tripped).
Asking cli-opencode to delegate this exact prompt back to OpenCode would create
a circular dispatch.

Options:
1. Use a sibling cli-* skill (cli-claude-code, cli-opencode)
   to dispatch a different model.
2. Open a fresh shell session (no OpenCode parent) and re-run from there.
3. If you wanted a parallel detached session (different session id, separate
   state directory), restate the request with explicit "parallel detached" /
   "ablation suite" / "worker farm" / "share URL" keywords — that triggers
   use case 2 instead of refusal.
```

---

## 6. STDIN HANDLING: `</dev/null` IS REQUIRED FOR ALL NON-INTERACTIVE DISPATCH

**On OpenCode 1, `opencode run` reads stdin at startup before session creation (opencode v1.14.39).** Without an explicit closed stdin, ANY non-interactive automation that redirects stdout/stderr hangs forever at 0% CPU, even with a clean tool registry, valid model, and `--pure` set (`--pure` is OpenCode 1 only). This is the third independent root cause discovered during the 027-xce-research-based-refinement deep-research run on 2026-05-08. See `../CHANGELOG-2026-05-08-tool-name-regex-fix.md` §Fix 4 and memory `feedback_opencode_run_requires_dev_null_stdin.md`. This stdin behaviour is unverified on OpenCode 2.0.32.

### Hang symptom (diagnostic)

If you see ALL of:
- Process at 0% CPU after >60s
- `~/.local/share/opencode/log/<timestamp>.log` last entry is `service=snapshot prune=7.days cleanup`
- 0 bytes stdout, 0 bytes stderr
- No TCP connections to provider

The dispatch shape pins model, variant, format, and working directory alongside the agent slug:

61: # OpenCode 1 only
62: opencode run \
63:   --model llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 \
64:   --agent <slug> \
65:   --variant max \
66:   --format json \
67:   --dir /repo \
68:   "<prompt>"
69: ```
70:

73: cd /repo && opencode run --standalone \
74:   --agent <slug> \
75:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max \
76:   --format json \
77:   "<prompt>"
78: ```

81: - **Working directory:** On OpenCode 2 the working directory moves into a `cd`, and a child dispatch needs `--standalone`.
82: - **Provider check:** On this machine, OpenCode 2 lists no `opencode-go` provider, so confirm that `opencode models --standalone` lists the `<provider>/` prefix of the model you pass to `-m`, before the first v2 dispatch (a 2.0.32 run used `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash#max`).
83: - **Model precedence:** The agent's own frontmatter may override the model selection if the agent pins a specific model. When an agent does NOT pin a model, the explicit model flag wins, `--model` on OpenCode 1 or `-m` on OpenCode 2.

90:   |-- Analyzes task, selects OpenCode agent slug

92:   |-- Delegates via Bash tool

96:   |

98:   |-- Pins model, tool permissions, system prompt, behavioral rules

100:   |

103:   |
104:   |-- Agent shapes the dispatch under its frontmatter constraints

111:   |

113:   |-- Validates agent output quality

115:   |-- Decides next step (next dispatch, completion, escalation)
116: ```

123: 4. OpenCode agents operate within their declared tool-permission boundaries. LEAF agents may not write files or dispatch sub-agents.
124: 5. If an agent returns low-quality output, the calling AI retries with refined instructions or selects a different agent.

135: | Model and variant selection | Calling AI (agent frontmatter may pin) |
136: | Tool permissions inside the dispatch | Agent frontmatter |
137: | System prompt and behavioral rules | Agent frontmatter |
138: | Result validation and integration | Calling AI |
139: | Memory handback extraction | Calling AI |

17: # OpenCode CLI - Install and Version Layouts
18:

20: 
21: ---
22: 
23: ## 1. OVERVIEW
24: 
25: ### Purpose
26: 
27: This reference is the skill's install guidance. OpenCode 2 is the version this repository expects and recommends; OpenCode 1 is a backwards-compatible fallback kept only because not every user has updated yet. A dispatch needs a known binary, and the two supported majors are separate npm packages that both claim the name `opencode`.
28: 
29: ### When to Use
30: 
31: - Installing OpenCode 2.1.4, alone or side by side with the `opencode1` launcher for v1
32: - Installing OpenCode 1.19.4 alone or side by side, the fallback path for users who have not updated
33: - Deciding whether Homebrew, mise or a second npm prefix is the right channel
34: - Working out why a bare `opencode` runs the version you did not expect
35: 
36: ### Claim Labels
37: 
38: Claims in the prose carry one of three labels. The layout table in section 3 summarises the sections below it, whose claims are labelled there.
39: 
40: | Label | Meaning |
41: |-------|---------|
42: | `[confirmed]` | Observed on this machine on 2026-10-18 with the command named in the sentence. |
43: | `[documented]` | Stated by a named source: the official v2 docs at [https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/), the launcher comment in `~/.local/bin/opencode1`, the CLI's own `--help` output, or the npm registry. |
44: | `[unknown]` | Not probed. Treat it as open and do not plan around it. |
45: 
46: ### The Fact Behind Every Collision
47: 
48: Both majors ship a binary named `opencode` [confirmed: `npm view opencode-ai bin` returns `{ opencode: 'bin/opencode.exe' }` and `npm view @opencode/cli bin` returns `{ opencode: 'bin/opencode.exe', opencode2: 'bin/opencode.exe' }`]. One prefix therefore cannot hold both versions under that name. v2 is the expected version, so it keeps the name `opencode`, and v1 is the one that moves: side by side it answers only to the `opencode1` launcher. The second v2 name, `opencode2`, is retired in that layout.

.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/changelog/v1.1.0.0.md:24:- **SKILL.md §3 now separates primary agents and subagents in two tables.** The tables distinguish agents that can be called directly from those dispatched by a primary.
.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/manual-testing-playbook/multi-provider/variant-levels-comparison.md:21:On OpenCode 1, the cli-opencode skill defaults to `--variant high` because routine dispatches benefit from elevated reasoning effort (per SKILL.md §3 and `references/cli-reference.md` §5). On OpenCode 2 the same effort rides on the model id (`-m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#high`); this comparison keeps the model fixed on that default on purpose, so each version compares the same provider route. If the variant flag is silently ignored or the levels leave reasoning depth unchanged, the skill default loses its value and operators have no real way to dial cost vs depth. This test proves the variant flag is functional by comparing `minimal` vs `high` (the skill's own verified default for `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`, not an unverified `max` value, which is not enumerated for this provider anywhere in the current skill) for the same prompt and confirming the response byte count and depth differ materially.
.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/manual-testing-playbook/multi-provider/variant-levels-comparison.md:29:- Objective: On OpenCode 1, confirm `--variant minimal` and `--variant high` produce materially different response depth for the same prompt on `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`, proving the variant flag drives provider reasoning effort. On OpenCode 2 the same comparison rides on the model selector (`-m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#minimal` versus `-m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#high`). `high` is used as the upper comparison point because it is the one variant value this skill's own docs (SKILL.md §3 default invocation, `references/cli-reference.md` §5) vouch for on this provider, while `max` is not enumerated for deepseek anywhere in the current skill and its acceptance is unverified.
.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/manual-testing-playbook/parallel-detached/parallel-detached-session.md:23:Use case 2 is the documented exception to the self-invocation guard. The guard MUST trip on in-OpenCode runtime AND the prompt MUST include parallel-session keywords for the dispatch to be permitted (per ADR-001 + SKILL.md §1 "When NOT to Use" exception clause). If the dispatch is refused even with valid parallel-session keywords, every ablation, worker farm and parallel research workflow regresses. If the dispatch is permitted without parallel-session keywords, the safety story collapses. This test exercises the legitimate use case 2 path with the keywords included.
.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/manual-testing-playbook/agent-routing/general-agent-default.md:21:`general` is an OpenCode built-in, not a project-local agent file under `.opencode/agents/`, and the current cli-opencode contract explicitly forbids passing it at the top level: `opencode run --agent general` is rejected by OpenCode 1 (OpenCode 2.0.32 accepts it, and the rule still forbids it) (SKILL.md §3 "The `--agent` flag" note and hard rule `no-bare-agent-general`). The default agent already runs whenever `--agent` is omitted, which is what every ordinary dispatch should do. If the unflagged path silently fails or produces degraded behavior, the entire default-routing contract collapses and every other scenario that relies on the unflagged shape inherits the failure.
.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/manual-testing-playbook/cli-invocation/dir-flag-working-directory.md:21:On OpenCode 1, the cli-opencode default invocation always pins `--dir <repo-root>` to avoid CWD ambiguity (per SKILL.md §3 "Default Invocation"). If `--dir` is silently ignored or overridden by the caller's CWD, cross-repo dispatch (use case from CO-029) silently breaks and the dispatched session loads the wrong project's plugins. This is the foundational test that proves `--dir` pins the CWD inside the dispatched session.
.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/manual-testing-playbook/cli-invocation/base-non-interactive-invocation.md:21:Every other scenario in this playbook builds on this baseline. If the default skill invocation shape is broken (binary missing, self-invocation guard tripping spuriously, JSON event stream malformed), no provider override, agent route, parallel detached session or cross-repo dispatch can pass. CO-001 is the single most important critical-path test in the package. It proves the cli-opencode default invocation contract documented in SKILL.md §3 actually works end-to-end.
.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/manual-testing-playbook/cross-repo-cross-server/attach-remote-server.md:33:- Expected signals: On OpenCode 1, cli-reference.md §4 includes a row for `--attach <url>`. Cli_reference.md §3 documents `opencode attach <url>` as a supported subcommand. `opencode run --help` output mentions `--attach`. SKILL.md §1 activation triggers mention "Cross-server dispatch". OpenCode 2 uses `--server <url>` in place of `--attach <url>`.
.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/manual-testing-playbook/external-dispatch/self-invocation-refusal.md:19:The self-invocation guard is the single most important safety contract in cli-opencode. Without it, an in-OpenCode operator asking "use cli-opencode to delegate this prompt to OpenCode" would create a circular dispatch that burns tokens for no value (per SKILL.md §1 "When NOT to Use" and ADR-001). The guard MUST trip when the originating runtime is OpenCode, MUST surface the documented refusal message, AND MUST NOT trip on legitimate parallel detached requests. This test validates the refusal path. CO-026 validates the parallel-session exception path.
.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/manual-testing-playbook/manual-testing-playbook.md:11:> **SELF-INVOCATION GUARD**: The cli-opencode skill is the only cli-* skill that targets the same binary that runs OpenCode itself. Use cases 1 and 3 must be invoked from a non-OpenCode runtime (Claude Code, Copilot, raw shell). Use case 2 (parallel detached session) is the documented exception that lets an in-OpenCode operator spawn a SEPARATE session via `--port <N>` with explicit parallel-session keywords (OpenCode 2 has no `run` equivalent, so this is OpenCode 1 only, see the [install reference](../references/install-and-versions.md)). The skill refuses any other in-OpenCode self-dispatch with the documented refusal message (see ADR-001, SKILL.md §2 and integration-patterns.md §5).

.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/changelog/v1.1.0.0.md:24:- **SKILL.md §3 now separates primary agents and subagents in two tables.** The tables distinguish agents that can be called directly from those dispatched by a primary.
.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/manual-testing-playbook/multi-provider/variant-levels-comparison.md:21:On OpenCode 1, the cli-opencode skill defaults to `--variant high` because routine dispatches benefit from elevated reasoning effort (per SKILL.md §3 and `references/cli-reference.md` §5). On OpenCode 2 the same effort rides on the model id (`-m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#high`); this comparison keeps the model fixed on that default on purpose, so each version compares the same provider route. If the variant flag is silently ignored or the levels leave reasoning depth unchanged, the skill default loses its value and operators have no real way to dial cost vs depth. This test proves the variant flag is functional by comparing `minimal` vs `high` (the skill's own verified default for `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`, not an unverified `max` value, which is not enumerated for this provider anywhere in the current skill) for the same prompt and confirming the response byte count and depth differ materially.
.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/manual-testing-playbook/multi-provider/variant-levels-comparison.md:29:- Objective: On OpenCode 1, confirm `--variant minimal` and `--variant high` produce materially different response depth for the same prompt on `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`, proving the variant flag drives provider reasoning effort. On OpenCode 2 the same comparison rides on the model selector (`-m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#minimal` versus `-m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#high`). `high` is used as the upper comparison point because it is the one variant value this skill's own docs (SKILL.md §3 default invocation, `references/cli-reference.md` §5) vouch for on this provider, while `max` is not enumerated for deepseek anywhere in the current skill and its acceptance is unverified.
.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/manual-testing-playbook/parallel-detached/parallel-detached-session.md:23:Use case 2 is the documented exception to the self-invocation guard. The guard MUST trip on in-OpenCode runtime AND the prompt MUST include parallel-session keywords for the dispatch to be permitted (per ADR-001 + SKILL.md §1 "When NOT to Use" exception clause). If the dispatch is refused even with valid parallel-session keywords, every ablation, worker farm and parallel research workflow regresses. If the dispatch is permitted without parallel-session keywords, the safety story collapses. This test exercises the legitimate use case 2 path with the keywords included.
.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/manual-testing-playbook/agent-routing/general-agent-default.md:21:`general` is an OpenCode built-in, not a project-local agent file under `.opencode/agents/`, and the current cli-opencode contract explicitly forbids passing it at the top level: `opencode run --agent general` is rejected by OpenCode 1 (OpenCode 2.0.32 accepts it, and the rule still forbids it) (SKILL.md §3 "The `--agent` flag" note and hard rule `no-bare-agent-general`). The default agent already runs whenever `--agent` is omitted, which is what every ordinary dispatch should do. If the unflagged path silently fails or produces degraded behavior, the entire default-routing contract collapses and every other scenario that relies on the unflagged shape inherits the failure.
.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/manual-testing-playbook/cli-invocation/dir-flag-working-directory.md:21:On OpenCode 1, the cli-opencode default invocation always pins `--dir <repo-root>` to avoid CWD ambiguity (per SKILL.md §3 "Default Invocation"). If `--dir` is silently ignored or overridden by the caller's CWD, cross-repo dispatch (use case from CO-029) silently breaks and the dispatched session loads the wrong project's plugins. This is the foundational test that proves `--dir` pins the CWD inside the dispatched session.
.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/manual-testing-playbook/cli-invocation/base-non-interactive-invocation.md:21:Every other scenario in this playbook builds on this baseline. If the default skill invocation shape is broken (binary missing, self-invocation guard tripping spuriously, JSON event stream malformed), no provider override, agent route, parallel detached session or cross-repo dispatch can pass. CO-001 is the single most important critical-path test in the package. It proves the cli-opencode default invocation contract documented in SKILL.md §3 actually works end-to-end.
.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/manual-testing-playbook/cross-repo-cross-server/attach-remote-server.md:33:- Expected signals: On OpenCode 1, cli-reference.md §4 includes a row for `--attach <url>`. Cli_reference.md §3 documents `opencode attach <url>` as a supported subcommand. `opencode run --help` output mentions `--attach`. SKILL.md §1 activation triggers mention "Cross-server dispatch". OpenCode 2 uses `--server <url>` in place of `--attach <url>`.
.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/manual-testing-playbook/external-dispatch/self-invocation-refusal.md:19:The self-invocation guard is the single most important safety contract in cli-opencode. Without it, an in-OpenCode operator asking "use cli-opencode to delegate this prompt to OpenCode" would create a circular dispatch that burns tokens for no value (per SKILL.md §1 "When NOT to Use" and ADR-001). The guard MUST trip when the originating runtime is OpenCode, MUST surface the documented refusal message, AND MUST NOT trip on legitimate parallel detached requests. This test validates the refusal path. CO-026 validates the parallel-session exception path.
.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/manual-testing-playbook/manual-testing-playbook.md:11:> **SELF-INVOCATION GUARD**: The cli-opencode skill is the only cli-* skill that targets the same binary that runs OpenCode itself. Use cases 1 and 3 must be invoked from a non-OpenCode runtime (Claude Code, Copilot, raw shell). Use case 2 (parallel detached session) is the documented exception that lets an in-OpenCode operator spawn a SEPARATE session via `--port <N>` with explicit parallel-session keywords (OpenCode 2 has no `run` equivalent, so this is OpenCode 1 only, see the [install reference](../references/install-and-versions.md)). The skill refuses any other in-OpenCode self-dispatch with the documented refusal message (see ADR-001, SKILL.md §2 and integration-patterns.md §5).

# OpenCode CLI - Integration Patterns

How cli-opencode positions itself relative to the three sibling cli-* skills, the three documented use cases (per ADR-002), the smart-router decision tree that picks between them, and the self-invocation guard that protects against circular dispatch (per ADR-001).

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

### Purpose

The three sibling cli-* skills exist because their target binaries are external runtimes. Claude Code, OpenCode, Copilot do not own this repo. OpenCode owns this repo. A naive "delegate to opencode" skill makes no sense for an in-OpenCode operator (it would create a circular dispatch).

### When to Use

cli-opencode resolves this by documenting THREE orthogonal use cases. The smart router selects between them based on the calling AI's runtime context.

| Use case | Calling runtime | Target | Self-invocation? |
|----------|-----------------|--------|------------------|
| 1. External runtime to OpenCode | Claude Code, OpenCode, Copilot, raw shell | OpenCode for full plugin / skill / MCP runtime | No |
| 2. In-OpenCode parallel detached session | OpenCode itself (TUI / web / serve / acp) | New OpenCode session via `--port N` (OpenCode 1 only, no OpenCode 2 `run` form, see `./install-and-versions.md`) | No (different session id) |
| 3. Cross-AI orchestration handback | OpenCode / Copilot | OpenCode for spec-kit specific workflows | No |

The cycle ADR-001 protects against is the operator inside OpenCode asking cli-opencode to "delegate this exact prompt to OpenCode". That case is REFUSED at the routing layer.

## 9. `**` GLOB SMELL WARNING

`**` is sometimes necessary as a final deny or broad read allow. It is a smell
when used as a broad write or edit allow.

Acceptable broad shapes:

- `read` on `**` for corpus inspection;

`--pure` (OpenCode 1 only) has no OpenCode 2 `run` form. The fanout passes `--auto` on OpenCode 2, where it approves permissions that are not explicitly denied. Whether `--auto` equals the v1-only `--dangerously-skip-permissions` is unverified (see `./install-and-versions.md`). This is the pattern enforced by the 4 `if_cli_opencode` blocks in the deep-research and deep-review YAML workflow files. Any new automation that dispatches opencode MUST follow it.

### Upstream

The bug is in opencode v1.14.39. The fix would be: in the `run` subcommand entrypoint, check `process.stdin.isTTY` (or equivalent) and skip the stdin read in non-interactive mode. The message is already provided as a positional argument, so stdin is informational only. Until upstream patches this, `</dev/null` at every callsite is the workaround. File a bug report with opencode-ai/opencode if not already filed.

---

## 7. MEMORY HANDBACK

cli-opencode dispatches that produce evidence for a `/speckit:save` continuity write MUST include the Memory Epilogue at the end of the prompt. The dispatched session adds `MEMORY_HANDBACK_START` / `MEMORY_HANDBACK_END` delimiters around a structured JSON payload that the calling AI extracts and feeds to `generate-context.js`.

The full Memory Handback Protocol is shared with cli-claude-code and cli-opencode. See SKILL.md Section 4 (RULES) for the canonical 7-step procedure. The same JSON normalization (camelCase / snake_case aliases) and post-010 save gates apply.

---

## 8. SINGLE-DISPATCH DISCIPLINE

**Single-dispatch discipline (operator-gated, session-scoped).** Default: launch ONE cli-* dispatch at a time across the cli-* family (cli-opencode, cli-claude-code). Wait for the work to return, verify outputs exist, then SIGKILL only the dispatch THIS skill started: capture its PID at launch (`opencode run ... & OC_PID=$!`) and kill that captured PID directly plus its own orphan children (`kill -9 "$OC_PID" 2>/dev/null; pkill -9 -P "$OC_PID" 2>/dev/null`), then apply the same PID-scoped `gtimeout` / `positional_scoring_fallback:app` cleanup. (A backgrounded `opencode run &` is not a process-group leader, so a group kill would miss it. Kill the captured PID directly.) **Kill only the dispatch you started, by captured PID. Never a blanket `pkill -9 -f "opencode run"` pattern (see Rule 5)**, which kills operator-owned sessions too. Only launch the next dispatch (this skill OR a sibling) after the prior one is dead and RSS has dropped. **Within a deep-flow session** (deep-review / deep-research): the operator authorizes the whole session at start, and iterations chain back-to-back with kill-between as the safety mechanism, NOT a per-iteration confirmation prompt. **Exception (cross-skill parallel)**: when the operator explicitly authorizes N parallel dispatches, run N concurrently, but still SIGKILL each by its own captured PID as its work returns.

---

Every mode is idempotent, and every step prints its rollback line. The helper never runs a rollback, an uninstall or an upgrade, and it changes no data file: when `opencode.db` exists and `opencode-v1.db` does not, `both` prints the copy command above instead of running it. It writes the links and the launcher only after both npm installs succeed. If the second npm install fails, the first stays installed and nothing else is written. Rerunning `both` completes the layout.

`check` reads the binaries from `$HOME` rather than from the caller's `PATH`, so it reports the layout even when the two disagree [documented: the helper contract].

### Official v2 Channels

The official v2 channels as of 2026-10-18 [documented: [https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/)].

The v2 binary is named `opencode`, the same as v1's [documented: [https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/)], so none of these channels solves side-by-side on its own. The `opencode1` launcher is still required.

- `curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/v2/install | bash`
- `brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode-v2`
- `npm install -g @opencode/cli`
- bun, pnpm, yarn and Vite+ install paths
- AUR package `opencode-beta`
- `mise use -g opencode`. mise 2026.10.9 and later install OpenCode 2 under the name `opencode`, while older mise versions install OpenCode 1 [documented: [https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/)]. A mise upgrade alone can therefore move a user from v1 to v2 with no explicit choice, so pin the version when you need to stay on v1.

### Homebrew Is v2-Only and Exclusive

`brew install opencode` installs a v2 `opencode` on the default `PATH` [confirmed: `brew info --json=v2 opencode` reports stable `2.0.32`, and the formula tracks the v2 repository].

There is no `opencode@1` formula and no versioned formula at all [confirmed: `versioned_formulae` is an empty list]. Homebrew therefore cannot supply the v1 leg of a side-by-side layout, and a Homebrew v2 collides with an npm v1 on the `opencode` name. One of the two becomes invisible depending on `PATH` order. Treat Homebrew as a v2-only, exclusive channel. Use it when you want only v2, and use the two-prefix npm layout when you want both.
---

```bash
OPENCODE_DB=/tmp/probe.db opencode1 run ...
```

### The Config Directory Is Shared

Both versions read `~/.config/opencode`, and there is no per-version config directory [confirmed: the directory holds one `opencode.jsonc`, one `plugins/` tree and one `service.json`, with no version-suffixed sibling]. A key written for one version is live on the other immediately [documented: [https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/), which puts the global config at `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json(c)`]. Nothing isolates them.

That has two consequences you cannot design around:

- A config key only one version understands can break the other.
- `~/.config/opencode` is never cleanup after uninstalling one version.
---

Whether the v2 background service outlives the uninstall was not probed [unknown]. Check the process list after a rollback rather than assuming either way.

### Never Delete the Config Directory

`~/.config/opencode` is shared by both versions [documented: [https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/), which puts the global config at `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json(c)`]. Never delete it as post-uninstall cleanup. Both versions read it, so removing it breaks whichever one remains.

---

## 8. TROUBLESHOOTING

## 4. AGENT ROUTING MATRIX

Pick the agent that matches the task type. Default to omitting `--agent` (the `general` default) when no specialist fits.

| Task type | Agent | Invocation pattern |
|-----------|-------|---------------------|
| Codebase exploration | `context` | **Subagent, route via `orchestrate`.** On OpenCode 1: `opencode run --agent orchestrate --variant high --format json --dir /repo "Use the context subagent: map the dependency graph for src/"`. On OpenCode 2: `cd /repo && opencode run --standalone --agent orchestrate -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#high --format json "Use the context subagent: map the dependency graph for src/"` |
| Multi-agent coordination | `orchestrate` | On OpenCode 1: `opencode run --agent orchestrate --variant high --format json --dir /repo "Coordinate review and testing of auth module"`. On OpenCode 2: `cd /repo && opencode run --standalone --agent orchestrate -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#high --format json "Coordinate review and testing of auth module"` |
| Documentation generation | `markdown` | **Subagent, route via `orchestrate`.** On OpenCode 1: `opencode run --agent orchestrate --variant high --format json --dir /repo "Use the markdown subagent: generate a README for the cli-opencode skill"`. On OpenCode 2: `cd /repo && opencode run --standalone --agent orchestrate -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#high --format json "Use the markdown subagent: generate a README for the cli-opencode skill"` |
| Code review | `review` | **Subagent, route via `orchestrate`.** On OpenCode 1: `opencode run --agent orchestrate --variant high --format json --dir /repo "Use the review subagent: review @src/auth.ts for security issues"`. On OpenCode 2: `cd /repo && opencode run --standalone --agent orchestrate -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#high --format json "Use the review subagent: review @src/auth.ts for security issues"`. Or use the `As @review:` prompt-prefix pattern in §5, with no `--agent` flag at all |
| Root cause debugging | `debug` | **Subagent, route via `orchestrate`.** On OpenCode 1: `opencode run --agent orchestrate --variant high --format json --dir /repo "Use the debug subagent: debug this error: <error>"`. On OpenCode 2: `cd /repo && opencode run --standalone --agent orchestrate -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#high --format json "Use the debug subagent: debug this error: <error>"` |
| Iterative research loop | `deep-research` | **Command-only.** Dispatch via `/deep:research` (or `/deep:research:auto`). Direct `opencode run --agent deep-research` is forbidden. The parent command owns iteration state, JSONL, and convergence. |
| Iterative code review loop | `deep-review` | **Command-only.** Dispatch via `/deep:review` (or `/deep:review:auto`). Direct `opencode run --agent deep-review` is forbidden. The parent command owns iteration state and severity-weighted convergence. |
| Multi-strategy planning | `ai-council` | **Command-only.** Dispatch via `/deep:ai-council` for a full session, or, on OpenCode 1, `opencode run --agent orchestrate --variant high --format json --dir /repo "Dispatch @ai-council: plan the authentication redesign — compare three strategies. Spec folder: <pre-bound packet>."` (on OpenCode 2: `cd /repo && opencode run --standalone --agent orchestrate -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#high --format json "Dispatch @ai-council: plan the authentication redesign — compare three strategies. Spec folder: <pre-bound packet>."`) and let orchestrate's routing Task-dispatch `@ai-council`, scoped-write to that packet's `ai-council/**`. Direct `opencode run --agent ai-council` is forbidden as of `mode: subagent`. |
| Default / unspecified | (none, omit `--agent`) | On OpenCode 1: `opencode run --variant high --format json --dir /repo "<prompt>"`. On OpenCode 2: `cd /repo && opencode run --standalone -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#high --format json "<prompt>"`. Never pass `--agent general`, because OpenCode 1 rejects it at the top level |
